packages/contracts/tsconfig.json.content: `include: ["src"]` also pulls in the co-located test files (`src/index.test.ts`, `src/schema-validation.property.test.ts`). Since `build` runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json` with `declaration: true` (inherited from `../../tsconfig.base.json`), the build emits test JS and `.d.ts` files into `dist` (e.g. `dist/index.test.js`, `dist/*.test.d.ts`), which then get published with the package since `package.json` has no `files` allowlist. Those artifacts also carry a compile-time dependency on the `vitest` devDependency. Consider excluding test files from the build (or splitting a `tsconfig.build.json`).

packages/dj-core/tsconfig.json.content: The `include` covers all of `src`, which contains test files (`src/index.test.ts`, `src/beat-mapping.property.test.ts`). The base config's `exclude` only removes `node_modules`/`dist`, so `tsc -p tsconfig.json` will compile and emit these tests into `dist` (e.g. `dist/index.test.js`, `dist/*.test.d.ts`). Because `main`/`types` point at `dist/index.js`/`dist/index.d.ts` and there is no `files` allowlist in package.json, the test artifacts (which import the devDependency `vitest`) get shipped and their emitted declarations reference a non-runtime dependency. Exclude test files from the build (a separate test tsconfig or an explicit exclude).

packages/failover/vitest.config.ts.content: `readdirSync(workspaceSrc)` returns every entry under `packages/` (files and directories), and each one is unconditionally turned into an `@autolight/<name>` alias pointing at `<entry>/src/index.ts` without verifying that the entry is a package or that the target file exists. A stray non-package entry (a file such as `README.md`/`.DS_Store`, a `.cache`/`node_modules` dir) silently produces a bogus alias, and any package whose entry is not `src/index.ts` resolves to a nonexistent module, causing confusing import-resolution failures instead of a clear error. Consider filtering to directories that actually contain `src/index.ts` (or read the package's `exports`/`main`), so the mapping stays in sync with the real package layout.

packages/matter/tsconfig.json.content: `include` covers all of `src` and no `exclude` is declared, so the build script (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`, which emits into `dist` per package.json) also compiles and emits the test files (`src/binding.test.ts`, `controller.test.ts`, `mapping.test.ts`, `simulator.test.ts`) to `dist/*.test.js` / `*.test.d.ts`. Reproduce with `npm run build` in `packages/matter` and inspect `dist/`: you will get `binding.test.js` etc., each of which does `import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"`. Since `vitest` is only a devDependency, every published/bundled `dist` now contains modules that resolve a non-runtime dependency and will throw at import time if ever loaded (e.g. by consumers globbing `dist`, or by test/bundle tooling). Since `main`/`types` point at `dist`, the shipped artifact is polluted with test code. Add an explicit exclusion for test sources (re-adding the base `node_modules`/`dist` exclusions, since specifying `exclude` overrides inherited values).

packages/rekordbox-live/vitest.config.ts.content: The alias map is built from a raw `readdirSync(workspaceSrc)` without filtering entries to directories. Every entry in `packages/` (including any stray non-directory file such as `.DS_Store`, `README.md`, a lockfile, or a non-package folder) becomes an alias `@autolight/<entry>` pointing at a non-existent `<entry>/src/index.ts`. Because resolution warnings/errors from such bogus aliases can silently break or obscure imports during tests, this is fragile. The root `vitest.config.ts` already guards against this with `readdirSync(workspaceSrc, { withFileTypes: true }).filter((e) => e.isDirectory())`; this file should stay consistent with it. There is also no fallback if `workspaceSrc` is unreadable/missing — the config throws at load time and takes down the whole test run.

packages/show-director/tsconfig.json.content: `include: ["src"]` also matches `src/index.test.ts`, so `npm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`) emits `dist/index.test.js` / `dist/index.test.d.ts` into the build output. Since `package.json` has no `files` allowlist, those test artifacts get published, and the emitted `dist/index.test.js` imports `vitest` (a devDependency that is not part of the published package), leaving dangling/broken output in the shipped bundle. Consider excluding test files from the build config. Note `exclude` overrides the inherited base exclude, so re-list `node_modules`/`dist`.

packages/show-mixer/package.json.content: `@autolight/show-planner` and `@autolight/storage` are declared as runtime `dependencies`, but a scan of `packages/show-mixer/src` shows they are only imported from test files (`blackout.test.ts`, `pipeline.test.ts`). The shipped runtime entry `src/index.ts` only imports `@autolight/contracts`, `@autolight/dj-core`, `@autolight/renderer` and `./blend.js`. Keeping test-only packages in `dependencies` makes every consumer of this package install them unnecessarily and misrepresents the runtime surface. Move them to `devDependencies` (or remove if the test coupling is dropped).

`--passWithNoTests` lets `vitest run` exit 0 when no tests are collected. If test discovery ever breaks (e.g. the `vitest.config.ts` include/glob is changed, files are renamed, or the glob is narrowed), CI silently reports success for a package with zero executed tests, masking regressions. Prefer dropping the flag so a missing-test situation fails the run.

The `lint` script is byte-for-byte the same command as `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`), so `yarn lint` performs no linting at all. Lint-only defects (unused vars, forbidden patterns, rule violations) cannot be caught by this package's `lint` target even though the repo ships oxlint/eslint tooling. Point `lint` at the actual linter, or drop the script and rely on the root lint gate.
